brief: Goldman's Pasquariello says the S&P's 57bp weekly drop (SPW +80bps) masks much larger moves underneath: GS's GSPRHIMO momentum basket swung -30.19%/-13.67%/+26.96%/-18.60% July-October versus the S&P's -0.13%/+2.62%/-0.45%/-0.93%. His view: the primary bull trend stays intact but with less upside power and persistent sub-surface volatility, so he is not making big bets now. Q3 tech/cloud earnings disappointed because, even with hyperscaler capex intentions clearly not slowing, several large companies missed in the core of their business, reinforcing his 2027 view that the bull market continues but with less punch, since S&P earnings growth appears to have peaked and estimate-upgrade momentum has slowed versus recent cycles. For the next two months he thinks technicals favor bulls (downbeat sentiment, the year-end seasonal swing, length cleared over the past month), though bears could note the same case was made into late 2018. Separately: this week's Fed meeting was a non-event; oil has built risk premium into the midterms (COZ6 near highs) even as European equities, including the SMI, hit record highs; he agrees with raising commodities allocation (BCOM +28% YTD); and mega-cap tech had a rough three weeks, with the index's 4th-largest member posting its worst day ever as a public company.

cards.claim: The S&P fell 57bps this week while the equal-weighted S&P (SPW) rallied 80bps.
cards.anchor: a 57 bps setback in S&P (or an 80 bps rally in SPW)

cards.claim: Goldman's GSPRHIMO momentum basket returned -30.19% in July, -13.67% in August, +26.96% in September and -18.60% in October, far more volatile than the S&P's -0.13%, +2.62%, -0.45% and -0.93% over the same months.
cards.anchor: GSPRHIMO: -30.19% (July) ... -13.67% (August) ... +26.96% (September) ... -18.60% (October).

cards.claim: Goldman's base case is that the primary US equity bull trend remains intact, but the market will deliver less upside power and sub-surface volatility is here to stay.
cards.anchor: the primary bull trend remains intact, but the market will deliver less upside power, and sub-surface volatility is here to stay.

cards.claim: Pasquariello says he is not currently making 'big bets' even though they periodically appear, reflecting a cautious risk/reward stance.
cards.anchor: the big bets always appear, but I’m not making them right now.

cards.claim: Goldman says Q3 tech/cloud earnings will be remembered as a disappointment, despite a handful of cloud businesses compounding huge growth rates on huge revenue bases.
cards.anchor: despite a handful of cloud businesses that are compounding huge growth rates on huge denominators, Q3 results will be remembered as a disappointment.

cards.claim: Goldman says hyperscaler capex intentions are clearly not slowing down, yet a few large tech companies missed in the core of their business this earnings season.
cards.anchor: hyperscaler capex intentions are clearly NOT slowing down, a few of the big guns missed somewhere in the core of their business.

cards.claim: Goldman's view is that the bull market should continue into 2027 but with less punch, and after this week it has more confidence in that view.
cards.anchor: the bull market should continue in 2027, but it would pack less punch.

cards.claim: Goldman says S&P earnings have been superb but earnings growth increasingly appears to have peaked.
cards.anchor: it increasingly appears that earnings GROWTH has peaked.

cards.claim: Goldman says the rate of upgrades to S&P forward earnings estimates has clearly slowed relative to the last few reporting cycles.
cards.anchor: relative to the last few reporting cycles, the rate of upgrades to forward estimates has clearly slowed.

cards.claim: Goldman says the technicals favor the bulls specifically over the next two months.
cards.anchor: in thinking about the next two months specifically, I do think the bulls have one thing on their side: the technicals.

cards.claim: Goldman notes the seasonal swing is underway from the worst stretch of the year to the best stretch, supporting the near-term bull case.
cards.anchor: the seasonal swing is underway from the worst of the year (from mid-August to mid-October) to the best of the year

cards.claim: Goldman says the market has spent the past month clearing a very significant amount of length, supporting the near-term bull case.
cards.anchor: the market has spent the past month clearing a very significant amount of length.

cards.claim: Goldman says sentiment is unequivocally downbeat, a contrarian-bullish technical reason favoring equities over the next two months.
cards.anchor: sentiment is unequivocally downbeat (this is clear in off-the-shelf-measures and in my client conversations)

cards.claim: Goldman notes bears could counter the near-term bull technical case by pointing out the same argument was made heading into late 2018.
cards.anchor: the bears could argue that the same was said into late 2018.

cards.claim: Goldman says this week's Fed meeting was uneventful and conspicuously absent as a topic of conversation for stock operators.
cards.anchor: this week’s Fed meeting was uneventful. in fact, it was conspicuous in its absence as a topic of conversation for stock operators.

cards.claim: Goldman says the oil market has built up significant risk premium into the midterms, with the COZ6 contract at its highs.
cards.anchor: the oil market has clearly built up significant risk premium into the midterms (COZ6 is on the dead highs)
cards.topic: oil risk premium vs European equity rally

cards.claim: Goldman notes European equities rallied again this week, with the Swiss SMI index hitting record highs.
cards.anchor: European equities fought higher yet again this week (note SMI ripped to record highs)
cards.topic: oil risk premium vs European equity rally

cards.claim: Pasquariello agrees with the argument to increase allocation to commodities.
cards.anchor: I agree with the argument to increase your allocation to commodities.

cards.claim: The Bloomberg Commodity Index is up 28% year-to-date, and GS has made both a tactical and a structural bull case for commodities.
cards.anchor: BCOM +28% YTD, GS recently made both a tactical and a structural bull case

cards.claim: The 4th largest company in the S&P just had its single worst day ever as a public company, amid a tough three-week stretch for US mega-cap tech.
cards.anchor: the 4th largest company in the index just had its single worst day ever as a public company.
